Q: How does XSS work? A:

XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) works by injecting

malicious scripts into trusted web pages.

The browser executes them because they appear

to come from a trusted origin — bypassing

Same-Origin Policy from the inside.

3 types:

1. Stored XSS — payload saved in database,

executes for every visitor including admins

2. Reflected XSS — payload bounces back from

URL or form, requires a crafted link

3. DOM-based XSS — happens entirely client-side,

server never sees it, most WAFs are blind to it

Defense:

✅ Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'

✅ HttpOnly cookie flag

✅ Output encoding: < → < > → >

✅ Server-side sanitization (DOMPurify/bleach)

I made a full cinematic visual breakdown of

exactly how Stored XSS steals a session token

without touching the password:

youtube.com/@CAISD_Official

Q: is there any replacement for jinja? A:

what do you mean "transfer it to the other pages"?

jinja is mostly for generating HTML based on values in variables.

If you don't need to generate HTML based on values in variables then you can simply read(filename) in Python and concatenate strings, or include one string inside another string, and you will have full page. And it doesn't need any framework.

Q: Convert an int value to unicode A:

In Python 2 - Turn it into a string first, then into unicode.

str(integer).decode("utf-8")

Best way I think. Works with any integer, plus still works if you put a string in as the input.

Updated edit due to a comment: For Python 2 and 3 - This works on both but a bit messy:

str(integer).encode("utf-8").decode("utf-8")

Q: How to get the maximum and minimum value of an ordered set / ordered map? A:

As of rust 1.66.0 there are now first() and last() methods on BTreeSet and first_key_value() and last_key_values() methods on BTreeMap with the stabilization of feature map_first_last.

There are also extra methods that utilize the Entry API and other fanciness with the stabilized feature.

Q: How to calculate the area of irregular shapes programmatically? A:

You could partition the irregular polygon into smaller polygons with known area formulas, for instance by triangulation.
